summary: The prepared_gaia variant is a design + code Python implementation with an explicit in-process message broker and GAIA-style agents for detection, prediction, notification, disinfection, simulation, and GUI collection. It defines message types and structured message classes, which improves communication clarity over ad hoc strings. The implementation is still a simulation: sensor values and detections are random, notifications go to a GUI agent rather than the required real stakeholders, and the single 528-line main.py file concentrates too many responsibilities.

findings.description: The system defines explicit message type constants and structured message classes for sensor data, detection, prediction, notification, disinfection, and acknowledgements.
findings.evidence: prepared_gaia/implementation_workspace/roach_detection_mas/src/main.py:9-14 defines message type constants; lines 18, 47, 71, 94, 115, and 133 define message classes.

findings.description: The MessageBroker gives each registered agent its own queue and supports explicit send and receive operations.
findings.evidence: prepared_gaia/implementation_workspace/roach_detection_mas/src/main.py:153-173 defines MessageBroker with register_agent, send_message, and receive_message.

findings.description: Sensor readings include movement and timestamp data, but they are generated randomly rather than read from motion sensors.
findings.evidence: prepared_gaia/implementation_workspace/roach_detection_mas/src/main.py:19-25 defines SensorDataMessage with movement and timestamp; lines 195-198 generate random temperature, humidity, waste, and movement.

findings.description: Roach detections are simulated by random chance instead of being derived from incoming sensor movement data.
findings.evidence: prepared_gaia/implementation_workspace/roach_detection_mas/src/main.py:213-218 says the detector listens for sensor data, then uses random.random() > 0.8 for detection.

findings.description: Notification and disinfection behavior is modeled, but notifications are sent to a GUI agent instead of directly to a disinfection company, affected students, and administration.
findings.evidence: prepared_gaia/implementation_workspace/roach_detection_mas/src/main.py:347-350 sends NOTIFICATION_MSG to gui; lines 387-390 do the same for disinfection status.

findings.description: The system does not implement hotspot analysis for places with highest activity; it focuses on room_101 simulations and random detections.
findings.evidence: prepared_gaia/implementation_workspace/roach_detection_mas/src/main.py:415 sets self.room_id = 'room_101', and lines 421-430 generate sensor data for that single room.

findings.description: The main implementation file is larger than the review threshold and contains message models, broker, all agents, and system orchestration in one module.
findings.evidence: prepared_gaia/implementation_workspace/roach_detection_mas/src/main.py has 528 lines and defines MessageBroker, DetectionAgent, PredictionAgent, NotificationAgent, DisinfectionAgent, SimulationAgent, GUIAgent, and run_system.

findings.description: Long-running agent loops rely on print statements and sleep intervals, which is acceptable for a demonstration but weak for deployable monitoring.
findings.evidence: prepared_gaia/implementation_workspace/roach_detection_mas/src/main.py contains 14 print() calls and 15 sleep references; examples include lines 360, 400, 485, and 489.

missing_requirements: Actual motion-sensor ingestion is not implemented; movement and detection values are randomly generated.
No direct notification path to affected students, administration, and the disinfection company is implemented.
The system does not identify locations with the highest activity across monitored areas.
The student-facing bad-room-state instruction is not implemented as a stakeholder notification.
logical_inconsistencies: DetectionAgent comments say it listens for sensor data, but the detector uses random chance rather than parsing the sensor message content.
NotificationAgent comments say it listens for messages from WK and PK agents, but its behavior simulates a fixed warning and sends it to the GUI.
implementation_risks: Random detection and single-room simulation can mask gaps in the required monitoring workflow.
Notification behavior may appear complete in the GUI while required stakeholders receive no actual notification.
A 528-line orchestration file makes agent responsibilities and message-flow changes difficult to review safely.
Print-based runtime visibility is not sufficient for reliable operations or auditability.
